page_observations: THE PLAIN AND BOILER-HOUSING SUFFIXES ARE EXCHANGED HERE, AND THE DEPTH GOES WITH THEM. H.120 puts 01 and 00 on the PLAIN units and 31 and 30 on the BOILER HOUSINGS. So PF0601 is a boiler housing at d.62 while PJ0601 is an ordinary door at d.35, and PF0631 is an ordinary door while PJ0631 is a boiler housing - the same four digits, 270 mm apart. Anyone who derived a suffix would not merely mislabel a box, they would build it the wrong depth. AND THE FULL TALLY IS WORSE THAN A SWAP, which is why it is written out rather than summarised: 31 is a plain door at H.48, H.60, H.72, H.84 and H.96 and a boiler housing here. 30 is a plain pair at H.48 to H.96, AND the W.15 pull-out door at H.72, H.84 and H.96, and a boiler-housing pair here. 01 is a boiler housing at H.72, H.84 and H.96 and a plain door here. 00 IS A SINGLE TOP-HUNG DOOR AT H.36, H.48 AND H.60, a boiler-housing pair at H.72, H.84 and H.96, and a plain pair here - THREE meanings in one chapter. A first reading of this page called it a clean swap of a rule that held everywhere else; the tally is what a check produced when it was asked to list the ambiguous suffixes, and it shows the rule never held. THE SUFFIX IS A LOOKUP, READ THE ROW - and it is not even a lookup by family alone, since 30 needs the width digits too.

THE SECTION IS SHORT AND IT IS SHORT BY SUBTRACTION. No pull-out door, no folding doors, no compound of any kind, and no dish-drainer folding or compound either. H.120 offers the plain doors, one stacked pair, the corners, the niche and the boiler housings - and nothing that folds. It is the only wall family in the chapter with no folding position at all.

THE STACK IS EQUAL AGAIN AND THE LEAVES ARE 600. 60 + 60 = 120, dimensioned twice on the elevation, and the page prints the plural '2 top-hung doors'. That is the fourth family whose wording tracks its geometry. It stops at W.105 where every other family's stacked pair runs to 120.
THE ONE-DOOR TYPE GAINS A THIRD SHELF and starts at W.30 instead of W.15 - the only wall family whose plain door has no 150 width.

THE CORNER DIGITS MOVE AGAIN AND THIS TIME THEY RUN BACKWARDS. 70x70 is OJ0716 and 75x75 is OJ0714: the LARGER footprint takes the SMALLER digit. H.84 uses 13/15 and H.96 uses 23/25, both ascending. Three families, three pairs, one of them reversed. Gated on Elda Q7b, and recorded so nobody builds a corner code by analogy.
THE CORNER FILLER IS 10x5 HERE, against 5X5 at H.84 and H.96. Recorded with the gated position.

wall_door.description: Wall unit with door - 1 rh or lh door - 3 shelves
wall_door.notes: SUFFIX 01 ON A PLAIN DOOR, where H.72, H.84 and H.96 use it for a boiler housing 620 deep - see page_observations for the full tally. Three widths starting at 30: this is the only wall family whose plain door has no W.15. Three shelves, where H.84 and H.96 print two. ONE CODE, BOTH HANDS.

front_layout.note: One door covering the full front, hinged on a vertical edge. hinge_side per order.

wall_two_doors.description: Wall unit with doors - 2 doors - 3 shelves
wall_two_doors.notes: SUFFIX 00 ON A PLAIN PAIR - a third meaning for those digits, after the single top-hung door of H.36/H.48/H.60 and the boiler-housing pair of H.72/H.84/H.96. And ONE width where every other family prints two: H.120 has no 600 two-door unit at all.

front_layout.note: Two doors meeting in the middle.

wall_top_hung_doors_stacked.description: Wall unit with top-hung doors - 2 top-hung doors - 2 shelves - top door with Push-pull device
wall_top_hung_doors_stacked.notes: TWO EQUAL LEAVES OF 600, both dimensioned and summing to 1200, with the plural wording that has accompanied an equal pair in every family. Suffix 04, unswapped - the swap this page makes is confined to the plain-versus-boiler pairs. FIVE widths, stopping at 105: H.72, H.84 and H.96 all run to 120 here.

front_layout.note: 600 then 600, summing to the family's 1200. NO hinge_axis: one key cannot carry two leaves. Two slabs, which is also the handle count.

wall_boiler_housing_door.description: Wall boiler housing - 1 rh/lh door - custom-sized side panels
wall_boiler_housing_door.notes: SUFFIX 31 ON A BOILER HOUSING. PC0531, PD0531, PE0531, PG0531 and PF0531 are all ordinary doors at d.35; these two are 620 deep. Same widths as the other three families' boiler housings, and the opposite digits.

wall_boiler_housing_two_doors.description: Wall boiler housing - 2 doors - custom-sized side panels
wall_boiler_housing_two_doors.notes: SUFFIX 30 ON A BOILER HOUSING, where PF0630 and PF0930 are ordinary two-door wall units at d.35 and PF0130 is a pull-out door. The fourth family with boiler housings, and the first to give them the plain units' digits.
